blocks.text: STRATEGY · WAVE DECK · ATTENDED AUTONOMY
The Wave Deck — Idea & Strategy

items: four-Fable panel: vision · architecture · contrarian · horizon

content.value: The Wave Deck proposes rendering a running epic-cycle wave as a live, gated surface. This paper is the strategy that survived adversarial review: what the deck IS when it is great, the data spine that makes it unable to lie, the attack that nearly killed it, and the staged plan — one real gate, evidence-priced — that earns the rest. The reframe that holds it all: the deck is where Barkpark's three assets (agent host, task ledger, Papers) fuse into the one thing nobody else has —

children.value: a durable, replayable, human-governed record of autonomous work.

items.label: gates in the design → real in wave 1
cost of the minimum honest gate
items.value: ~1 day

blocks.text: The idea — attended autonomy as an instrument

content.value: A wave runs for hours; you spend ~8 minutes at gates. The deck's whole job is to make those the highest-information-density minutes of your day. Between gates it is ambient cinema — a calm stage saying “the machine is composed, you're not needed yet.” At a gate it snaps into a courtroom: the evidence for your choice on the table, verbatim, one gesture deep. And because every wave leaves a replayable decision log, the deck doubles as the wave's permanent artifact — portfolio, audit trail, and teaching tape in one.
Three signature moments exist nowhere else:

items.value: Verification refutes a premise and a build slice dies before anyone builds it — struck through live, the fleet dropping from five minds to four. The honesty doctrine in one animation.

You walk away mid-wave; the email says “Gate waiting — one claim unproven”; the deep link lands ON the gate; you read one proof and press proceed from your phone. Assembled entirely from parts wave 12 already shipped.
A colleague scrubs to gate 3, sees which slice you trimmed and your note explaining why, and understands a week of the project in four minutes. The decision log is a résumé of judgment.

blocks.text: The attack that nearly killed it — and what survived

content.value: The contrarian's verdict was
, and three of its attacks permanently shaped this strategy:

items.text: AskUserQuestion has no timeout; the deck's ?countdown=30 auto-pick is demo fiction with no harness primitive behind it. Five attended gates kill the 1.9-hour/34-agent/zero-input superpower; five auto gates are a decision log of defaults nobody chose. RESOLVED: one real gate at the one genuine judgment seam (post-Decide), unattended waves simply don't pass the arg, and countdown lives in the deck UI (answering the respond path with auto:true) — the lead never self-answers an attended gate.
items.title: A1 — Gates are blocking or decorative

items.text: bp-epic-cycle.workflow.js is the highest-leverage script in the repo, already damaged twice by worktree reverts. A per-phase split loses resume caching and the shared budget pool. RESOLVED by the iron rule: no gate ever lives inside the phase pipeline — the arch design keeps ONE monolithic script with early-return-at-missing-gate + resumeFromRunId; every branch is a pure suffix; nothing inserts before an executed call.
items.title: A2 — Blast radius on the money printer

items.text: Every byte the deck shows is already rendered somewhere (Paper = debrief, rail = live, board = ledger), and the same effort could ship wave-13's proven-pull items (search, notify wiring, mobile inbox). ACCEPTED: the deck skin waits for pull evidence; the gate mechanism and event spine ship small, folded into the near-term plan; wave-13's mobile inbox is what makes remote gates real anyway.
items.title: A3/A4 — Redundancy + opportunity cost

items.text: The deck was born as a scripted pitch, and the 426KB HTML port sits outside the theme-system's derive-only law — it can never ship as product code. ACCEPTED: the port is a choreography spec and a sales demo (P0, done, zero further cost); any shipped deck UI is re-authored on the token manifest, priced honestly as the largest slice, and gated on the go-signal.
items.title: A6/A7 — Demo-driven development + the skin

content.value: Its claim that the gate mechanism requires splitting the workflow (A2) was defused by the architecture spec's early-return design — one script, cache-preserved, iron rule honored. And its “fold everything into wave-13, file no epic” bottom line under-prices the horizon evidence: the seven schema decisions below cannot be backfilled, and deferring them costs the audit-trail product its history. The synthesis keeps the contrarian's sizing and evidence bar, not its shutdown.

blocks.text: Governance — kill-signals and the three-month test

items.value: after 3 attended waves, if the human never once overrides the default, gates are theater — delete the arg and cite this paper.
unattended waves must keep running end-to-end at current grade with zero epic-cycle regressions attributable to gate/projector plumbing.
deck investment beyond Stage 3 requires observed reach-for-it behavior, not vibes — opens during live waves, answers from the phone, a replay shared.
Stage 3's wave-12 acid test must fill every populated scene from structured data with zero prose parsing.
a deck-owned notification path (ride needs-you, permanently), a gate inside the phase pipeline, a scene not anchored in a record, prose parsing as infrastructure.

content.value: Ship the judgment seam, not the theater: one real gate where the human's choice is genuine, a spine that cannot lie, seven fields that keep the governance product possible — and let the cinema earn its screen.

blocks.text: Decisions to ratify

items.value: Adopt the staged plan: Stages 0–1 fold into the near-term plan beside wave-13 quick wins; Stages 2–3 as a small epic wave; deck surface gated on pull evidence.
G3 (post-Decide) is the one real gate in wave 1; G1/G2 stay auto (self-correction evidence D63/D68); G4/G5 remain the lead's existing boundaries.
Ratify the seven irreversible schema decisions and the experience laws as standing rules for all deck work.
The 426KB zen port is a spec + sales demo, never shipped code; any shipped surface is re-authored on the token manifest.

STRATEGY · WAVE DECK · ATTENDED AUTONOMY

The Wave Deck — Idea & Strategy

studio-claude-chat initiative · 2026-07-11 · four-Fable panel: vision · architecture · contrarian · horizon · companion to /papers/wave-deck-zen-handoff

The Wave Deck proposes rendering a running epic-cycle wave as a live, gated surface. This paper is the strategy that survived adversarial review: what the deck IS when it is great, the data spine that makes it unable to lie, the attack that nearly killed it, and the staged plan — one real gate, evidence-priced — that earns the rest. The reframe that holds it all: the deck is where Barkpark's three assets (agent host, task ledger, Papers) fuse into the one thing nobody else has — a durable, replayable, human-governed record of autonomous work.

4
Fable lenses, independently grounded
5→1
gates in the design → real in wave 1
0
new tables required
7
irreversible schema decisions
7
probes before the big build
~1 day
cost of the minimum honest gate

The idea — attended autonomy as an instrument

A wave runs for hours; you spend ~8 minutes at gates. The deck's whole job is to make those the highest-information-density minutes of your day. Between gates it is ambient cinema — a calm stage saying “the machine is composed, you're not needed yet.” At a gate it snaps into a courtroom: the evidence for your choice on the table, verbatim, one gesture deep. And because every wave leaves a replayable decision log, the deck doubles as the wave's permanent artifact — portfolio, audit trail, and teaching tape in one.

Three signature moments exist nowhere else:

1. The kill. Verification refutes a premise and a build slice dies before anyone builds it — struck through live, the fleet dropping from five minds to four. The honesty doctrine in one animation.
2. The gate that follows you. You walk away mid-wave; the email says “Gate waiting — one claim unproven”; the deep link lands ON the gate; you read one proof and press proceed from your phone. Assembled entirely from parts wave 12 already shipped.
3. The replay as artifact. A colleague scrubs to gate 3, sees which slice you trimmed and your note explaining why, and understands a week of the project in four minutes. The decision log is a résumé of judgment.
The experience laws (vision lens — each prevents a named failure mode)
(1) Animation is for waiting, never for deciding — any human arrival renders the gate instantly, fully dense; cinema lives in ambient idle and replay only. (2) AUTO-PICKED vs HUMAN-PICKED is permanent provenance in the decision log — replay never launders accountability — and a gate arriving with fresh negative evidence (refuted verdict, unproven claim, died agent) loses its countdown and escalates to attended. (3) Zen is the summary layer, always one gesture from the evidence layer — every rendered line expands in place to its verbatim source; a scene the data can't justify stays blank, and a scene the data exceeds gets an expand affordance, never truncation-as-lie. (4) Strict surface ownership: deck = the wave's state and gates; chat = the conversation; rail = the machinery. They deep-link, never mirror. (5) Derivation never invents state — one faked pulse and the instrument becomes a toy permanently.

The five gates — what the human must see to decide honestly

Cross-cutting: every option wears its cost in the sub-label (“proceed → ACCEPTS 1 UNPROVEN · LOGGED”), “recorded in the Paper” is a live link, and every summary line clicks through to verbatim source. A gate where you can't reach the evidence is a rubber stamp with mood lighting.

GateAfterMust seePower interactionWave 1
G1 Enough ground?DigestCoverage map with NOT-FOUND / UNREACHED as first-class; contradictions surfaced; died surveyors; your strategize questions answered?“Research more ↺” arrives pre-filled with the unreached corners as an editable round-2 planauto (fleet self-corrects — D63/D68 evidence)
G2 Proven enough?VerifyFull proof table: claim · command · observed line · verdict; UNPROVEN in amber, REFUTED showing what they killedClick a verdict → raw captured output; “verify more ↺” names the unproven claims in its sub-labelauto (candidate for gate #2 later)
G3 Approve the wave?DecideSlice slate as PUBLISHED tasks (live ledger links): model, criteria count, which proof each rests on; struck rows for slices that died pre-build; fleet cost shapeTrim ✂ in place — strike a slice, fleet count updates live, task stays filed with an honest noteREAL — the wave-1 gate
G4 Land it?Build+ReviewPer-slice terminal state (green + commit, or the builder's stamp VERBATIM); gate status per branch; reviewer fixes; grade WITH commentaryEvery slice row deep-links to its diff — the deck triages which diffs deserve your eyes, never replaces themexists already (the lead's merge boundary)
G5 Next wave?DebriefThe handoff text (next wave's inheritance), your five-decision log with AUTO/HUMAN provenance, the epic's remaining runwayThe handoff is EDITABLE before firing — redlining it makes “fire wave N+1” an act of steeringexists already (the lead's relaunch boundary)

The attack that nearly killed it — and what survived

The contrarian's verdict was build-different, mostly don't-build, and three of its attacks permanently shaped this strategy:

A1 — Gates are blocking or decorative
AskUserQuestion has no timeout; the deck's ?countdown=30 auto-pick is demo fiction with no harness primitive behind it. Five attended gates kill the 1.9-hour/34-agent/zero-input superpower; five auto gates are a decision log of defaults nobody chose. RESOLVED: one real gate at the one genuine judgment seam (post-Decide), unattended waves simply don't pass the arg, and countdown lives in the deck UI (answering the respond path with auto:true) — the lead never self-answers an attended gate.
A2 — Blast radius on the money printer
bp-epic-cycle.workflow.js is the highest-leverage script in the repo, already damaged twice by worktree reverts. A per-phase split loses resume caching and the shared budget pool. RESOLVED by the iron rule: no gate ever lives inside the phase pipeline — the arch design keeps ONE monolithic script with early-return-at-missing-gate + resumeFromRunId; every branch is a pure suffix; nothing inserts before an executed call.
A3/A4 — Redundancy + opportunity cost
Every byte the deck shows is already rendered somewhere (Paper = debrief, rail = live, board = ledger), and the same effort could ship wave-13's proven-pull items (search, notify wiring, mobile inbox). ACCEPTED: the deck skin waits for pull evidence; the gate mechanism and event spine ship small, folded into the near-term plan; wave-13's mobile inbox is what makes remote gates real anyway.
A6/A7 — Demo-driven development + the skin
The deck was born as a scripted pitch, and the 426KB HTML port sits outside the theme-system's derive-only law — it can never ship as product code. ACCEPTED: the port is a choreography spec and a sales demo (P0, done, zero further cost); any shipped deck UI is re-authored on the token manifest, priced honestly as the largest slice, and gated on the go-signal.
Where the contrarian lost
Its claim that the gate mechanism requires splitting the workflow (A2) was defused by the architecture spec's early-return design — one script, cache-preserved, iron rule honored. And its “fold everything into wave-13, file no epic” bottom line under-prices the horizon evidence: the seven schema decisions below cannot be backfilled, and deferring them costs the audit-trail product its history. The synthesis keeps the contrarian's sizing and evidence bar, not its shutdown.

The data spine — a deck that cannot lie

Three systems of record already exist: the ledger (slice truth: claims, criteria, evidence, closes — timestamped and structured), the wave Paper (the human story — prose, and it stays prose: never parsed), and the chat wire (live breathing: rail frames, ask rows). The spine adds exactly ONE new record — wave_event documents, append-only, one published doc per event — and forbids the deck from rendering anything not anchored in one of the four.

The honest-blank rule, mechanically: every projected leaf is a {value, source} pair where source points at a real record (event id, task field, paper anchor, rail key); a post-pass rejects any value without provenance — enforced by schema, not convention. Durable records decide WHICH scene; wire frames only animate WITHIN it. Replay and live are the same projection, which is the never-lie property.

The event vocabulary (v1, minimal — only what no other record holds): wave.opened (wish, epic, gate-policy snapshot), phase.entered/exited, fleet.dispatched/reported (coverage + proof counts — the survey-dots and proof-table scenes verbatim), gate.asked/answered (choice, note, by, auto), wave.closed/parked. Slice claims/stamps/closes are NOT events — the ledger and the existing mutation log own those. Emits are fire-and-forget: a failed emit logs and never blocks the wave; with the Waves plugin off, the wave runs identically.

The gate loop — one script, never split
The workflow gains args.gates: after a gated phase, if its answer is absent the script early-returns {awaiting: 'g3', gate_context, …partials}. The chat-hosted lead asks the gate as an AskUserQuestion ask row (the ask row IS the gate card), emits gate.answered, and re-invokes with resumeFromRunId — earlier phases cache-hit because their prompts never interpolate gate answers, and every branch (research-more, trim, redirect, park) is a pure suffix. Trim mutates the LEDGER (unpublish the slice task), never the script. Fallback if the resume probes fail: per-segment scripts with state forwarded via args — deterministic, no cache reliance.

The horizon — why the small version must be built precisely

Three bets, ranked, each with a cheap wave-1 position and a falsifier:

1. The gate ledger IS the product. “Run governed agent waves on your own infra” is the cleanest Barkpark Cloud flagship framing yet — what enterprises pay for is the audit trail: who answered, what they chose, what they wrote, what policy was in force, replayable. The countdown-default posture (attended by default, autonomy honest rather than blocked) is the differentiator itself. Falsifier: no second operator by Q4, or vendors ship first-party fleet-approval inboxes.
2. The wave is a document. Scene events + decision log + debrief = one durable artifact that is simultaneously a shareable replay, the compliance export, and a regression corpus for the deck itself. One projector, three doors. Falsifier: after 5+ real waves nobody has replayed one — then the projector remains a test harness, still worth having.
3. Generic names, no primitive. The gate vocabulary likely generalizes (deploys, migrations, improvement loops) — but building a gated-run primitive now violates the never-abstract-with-one-client rule the provider-horizon panel just ratified. Position with naming only: run_kind + gate_slug, never epic_cycle_*. The second gated pipeline decides whether the primitive exists.
Seven decisions wave 1 must get right — they cannot be backfilled
(1) decision_mode on every gate answer — human | countdown_default | auto_policy — plus nullable decided_by and decided_at; without it the audit story is retroactively dead. (2) The gate-policy snapshot stored WITH the wave — “what rules were in force when this was approved”; live config mutates. (3) A stable wave join key stamped on the chat session, the wave Paper, AND the slice tasks — the projector joins three ledgers; unstamped waves become unreplayable. (4) Generic event naming (run_kind). (5) :gate_waiting added to the needs-you vocabulary NOW — email inherits it today, Web Push in wave 13, for free. (6) Gate choice + note land in the Paper as a lead-written block via the PlanPapers projection pattern — human-readable face; the machine record is the event. (7) wave.replay.v1 — version the projection format from the first byte.

The plan — evidence-priced, one gate at a time

Every stage earns the next; the deck skin — the largest and least certain slice — ships last and only on demonstrated pull.

Stage 0
Probes (gates everything)
resumeFromRunId across an early-return run (highest risk in the whole design); resume after a chat-session reap; idempotent wave_event creates from workflow context; ask-row fidelity for options+note. ~2 days total.
S · probe-first discipline
→
Stage 1
The minimum honest gate (G3)
pause-after-Decide arg + resume path on the monolithic script; the lead asks ONE AskUserQuestion (approve / trim / redirect); choice+note → gate.answered event + Paper block; :gate_waiting rides needs-you → email deep-links to the ask row. Trim = ledger mutation. Unattended = don't pass the arg.
S-M · the contrarian's MHV, kept
→
Stage 2
Scene-event emission + the seven schema decisions
wave_event doc type, v1 vocabulary, fire-and-forget emits from the lead + phase agents, wave join key stamped across all three ledgers. Every future wave becomes deck-food.
M · irreversible fields land here
→
Stage 3
P1 projector — the falsifier
Pure projection to wave.replay.v1 scene JSON with enforced {value, source} provenance. Acid test: project wave 12 (ledger-only — honest blanks everywhere else) + one synthetic fully-evented wave. If any scene needs prose parsing, the mapping is falsified — record and stop.
M · handoff's own P1, taken seriously
→
GATED
Deck surface (P2 live + skin)
Go-signal: the owner reaches for the replay/gate surface unprompted during real waves, gate answers show non-default choices, and P1 filled every scene from structured data. Skin re-authored on the token manifest (the 426KB port is a spec, not shippable code). Until then the deck stays a stored spec + sales demo.
L · pull-evidence priced
Sequencing vs wave 13
Stages 0–1 are ~3 days and fold naturally into the near-term plan beside wave-13's quick wins (notify recipient-wiring makes the gate email real; the mobile inbox makes remote gates real). Stages 2–3 are a small wave of their own. The full deck does not jump the wave-13 queue — it earns its slot with the go-signal.

Governance — kill-signals and the three-month test

• Gate value: after 3 attended waves, if the human never once overrides the default, gates are theater — delete the arg and cite this paper.
• Throughput: unattended waves must keep running end-to-end at current grade with zero epic-cycle regressions attributable to gate/projector plumbing.
• Pull: deck investment beyond Stage 3 requires observed reach-for-it behavior, not vibes — opens during live waves, answers from the phone, a replay shared.
• Mapping: Stage 3's wave-12 acid test must fill every populated scene from structured data with zero prose parsing.
• Never: a deck-owned notification path (ride needs-you, permanently), a gate inside the phase pipeline, a scene not anchored in a record, prose parsing as infrastructure.

Ship the judgment seam, not the theater: one real gate where the human's choice is genuine, a spine that cannot lie, seven fields that keep the governance product possible — and let the cinema earn its screen.

Decisions to ratify

1. Adopt the staged plan: Stages 0–1 fold into the near-term plan beside wave-13 quick wins; Stages 2–3 as a small epic wave; deck surface gated on pull evidence.
2. G3 (post-Decide) is the one real gate in wave 1; G1/G2 stay auto (self-correction evidence D63/D68); G4/G5 remain the lead's existing boundaries.
3. Ratify the seven irreversible schema decisions and the experience laws as standing rules for all deck work.
4. The 426KB zen port is a spec + sales demo, never shipped code; any shipped surface is re-authored on the token manifest.

Sequencing vs wave 13 Stages 0–1 are ~3 days and fold naturally into the near-term plan beside wave-13's quick wins (notify recipient-wiring makes the gate email real; the mobile inbox makes remote gates real). Stages 2–3 are a small wave of their own. The full deck does not jump the wave-13 queue — it earns its slot with the go-signal.

Governance — kill-signals and the three-month test

  • Gate value: after 3 attended waves, if the human never once overrides the default, gates are theater — delete the arg and cite this paper.
  • Throughput: unattended waves must keep running end-to-end at current grade with zero epic-cycle regressions attributable to gate/projector plumbing.
  • Pull: deck investment beyond Stage 3 requires observed reach-for-it behavior, not vibes — opens during live waves, answers from the phone, a replay shared.
  • Mapping: Stage 3's wave-12 acid test must fill every populated scene from structured data with zero prose parsing.
  • Never: a deck-owned notification path (ride needs-you, permanently), a gate inside the phase pipeline, a scene not anchored in a record, prose parsing as infrastructure.

Ship the judgment seam, not the theater: one real gate where the human's choice is genuine, a spine that cannot lie, seven fields that keep the governance product possible — and let the cinema earn its screen.

Decisions to ratify

  1. Adopt the staged plan: Stages 0–1 fold into the near-term plan beside wave-13 quick wins; Stages 2–3 as a small epic wave; deck surface gated on pull evidence.
  2. G3 (post-Decide) is the one real gate in wave 1; G1/G2 stay auto (self-correction evidence D63/D68); G4/G5 remain the lead's existing boundaries.
  3. Ratify the seven irreversible schema decisions and the experience laws as standing rules for all deck work.
  4. The 426KB zen port is a spec + sales demo, never shipped code; any shipped surface is re-authored on the token manifest.
